question.prompt: Square pyramid \(ABCDE\) has base \(ABCD,\) which measures \(3\) cm on a side, and altitude \(\overline{AE}\) perpendicular to the base, which measures \(6\) cm. Point \(P\) lies on \(\overline{BE},\) one third of the way from \(B\) to \(E;\) point \(Q\) lies on \(\overline{DE},\) one third of the way from \(D\) to \(E;\) and point \(R\) lies on \(\overline{CE},\) two thirds of the way from \(C\) to \(E.\) What is the area, in square centimeters, of \(\triangle PQR?\)

solutions.title: A parallel square section
solutions.explanation:
Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are the same fraction of the way from \(E\) toward the base. A section parallel to the base through these points will reveal a convenient altitude of \(\triangle PQR\).

Let this plane meet \(AE\) at \(F\) and \(CE\) at \(T\). Since
\[
\frac{EP}{EB}=\frac{EQ}{ED}=\frac23,
\]
similar triangles in the lateral faces show that the section \(FPTQ\) is a square with side length \((2/3)\cdot3=2\). They also give
\[
EF=\frac23EA=4,
\qquad
ET=\frac23EC.
\]
Let \(S\) be the center of this square, where its diagonals \(FT\) and \(PQ\) meet. Thus \(S\) is the midpoint of \(FT\), and the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
PQ=\sqrt{2^2+2^2}=2\sqrt2.
\]
Because \(R\) is two thirds of the way from \(C\) to \(E\), we have \(ER=EC/3=ET/2\). Therefore \(R\) is the midpoint of \(ET\).

In \(\triangle EFT\), the segment \(RS\) joins the midpoints of \(ET\) and \(FT\). The midpoint theorem gives
\[
RS\parallel EF,
\qquad
RS=\frac12EF=2.
\]
The line \(EF\) is perpendicular to the base and hence also to the parallel square section. Thus \(RS\perp PQ\), making \(RS\) an altitude of \(\triangle PQR\).

Its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot PQ\cdot RS
=\frac12\cdot2\sqrt2\cdot2
=\boxed{2\sqrt2}\text{ cm}^2,
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Coordinates and an isosceles triangle
solutions.explanation:
The three perpendicular edges \(AB\), \(AD\), and \(AE\) make spatial coordinates convenient. Once we find the side lengths of \(\triangle PQR\), its area follows from an ordinary right triangle.

Choose
\[
A=(0,0,0),\quad B=(3,0,0),\quad C=(3,3,0),
\quad D=(0,3,0),\quad E=(0,0,6).
\]
To move a given fraction along a segment, add that fraction of each coordinate change to the starting coordinates. Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
P&=(3,0,0)+\frac13(-3,0,6)=(2,0,2),\\
Q&=(0,3,0)+\frac13(0,-3,6)=(0,2,2),\\
R&=(3,3,0)+\frac23(-3,-3,6)=(1,1,4).
\end{aligned}
\]
The spatial distance formula, obtained by applying the Pythagorean theorem in perpendicular directions, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
PQ^2&=(-2)^2+2^2+0^2=8,\\
PR^2&=(-1)^2+1^2+2^2=6,\\
QR^2&=1^2+(-1)^2+2^2=6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(PR=QR\), the triangle is isosceles. Let \(S\) be the midpoint of \(PQ\). Then \(RS\) is perpendicular to \(PQ\), and
\[
PS=\frac{PQ}{2}=\sqrt2,
\qquad
RS=\sqrt{PR^2-PS^2}=\sqrt{6-2}=2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
[\triangle PQR]=\frac12\cdot2\sqrt2\cdot2
=\boxed{2\sqrt2}\text{ cm}^2,
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
